note: Scores are judgment scores against this rubric. They are not market data. Every score is 1 to 5, and a higher score is always better for you.

criteria.name: Owner has no sales team
criteria.question: Does the owner personally do the selling, with nobody to set up or run sales software?

anchors.1: Most firms like this already have salespeople or a sales manager.
anchors.3: About half and half. The owner sells, but some firms have a rep.
anchors.5: The owner does nearly all the selling, between doing the actual work.

criteria.name: Value of one booked call
criteria.question: If one booked call turns into a customer, how much is that worth to this owner, compared with what they would pay you?

anchors.1: One new customer is small. It would take many to justify a monthly fee.
anchors.3: One new customer would plausibly cover a month of your fee.
anchors.5: One new customer is large or stays for years, so a few calls can justify the whole service.

criteria.name: How findable the buyers are
criteria.question: Can you list both sides from public sources: the owners who would pay you, and the customers you would book calls with? Score the weaker side.

anchors.1: One side has no public list and needs guesswork.
anchors.3: Both sides can be listed, with real manual research.
anchors.5: Both sides appear in public licence records, permits or directories.

criteria.name: How reachable by email
criteria.question: Do both sides have business email addresses they read? Score the weaker side.

anchors.1: One side mostly has no public business email (for example consumers or field crews).
anchors.3: Addresses exist, but they are often shared inboxes or read rarely.
anchors.5: Named people read their business email as part of the job.

criteria.name: Seasonality (steady all year scores high)
criteria.question: Can this owner take new calls in every month of the year?

anchors.1: Most of the year's buying happens in one season.
anchors.3: Clear busy and quiet periods, but work all year.

criteria.name: Compliance risk (low risk scores high)
criteria.question: How much could rules restrict the messages you send, or how you get paid?

anchors.1: Strict professional or referral rules. The usual pay per call deal may not be allowed.
anchors.3: Licensing or marketing rules that need written sign off from the client.
anchors.5: Only the ordinary rules for commercial email apply.

criteria.name: How crowded (a quiet market scores high)
criteria.question: How rarely do these owners hear this pitch from other outreach services?

anchors.1: Owners get pitched about leads constantly.
anchors.3: Some outreach services work this niche, but it is not saturated.
anchors.5: Almost nobody is doing this outreach.

global.label: The idea works in most countries, though the named lead sources are often US ones

us_first.label: Written for the US, needs local rules and sources elsewhere

us_only.label: Depends on US law or US programs
